newsitem.title: USA: Louisiana sweet crudes take beating in U.S. trade.
newsitem.headline: Louisiana sweet crudes take beating in U.S. trade.

text.p: Sweet Louisiana crude barrels were traded at sharply weaker prices Wednesday, pressured by a lack of refiner demand for fading June parcels.
Outright crude gained ground in line with technical buying on the NYMEX market, putting July West Texas Intermediate/Cushing around 25 cents higher at $21.80-90 a barrel late in the afternoon.
Front month June WTI/Cushing cash markets were pegged around 20 cents weaker than July, with prompt crude at $21.60-70 a barrel.
Louisiana grades lost steam as the session progressed, trading down to 20 cents under June WTI/Cushing. June LLS started the session flat to five cents under the benchmark.
Traders blamed LLS weakness on a slew of factors, none of which satisfied everyone entirely.
First, traders said foreign crude availability remained high in the Gulf, pressuring competing domestics.
Other reasons were shrinking pipeline space, sporadic refinery outages in the previous days and Brent-WTI arbitrage economics.

"There is the lack of storage on the Capline (pipeline), but what you really have is LLS returning to where it started. LLS has been artificially high in relation to the fundamentals," said a cash trader.
LLS sold down to 19 cents under June WTI, but talk had the sweet grade at 25 cents under level by late in the day.
Other action centered on Exchange for Physicals (EFPs), where premiums reached as high as 28 cents, and rested around 25 cents when June business expired Wednesday afternoon.
Traders expected word on the amount of foreign crude delivered against June NYMEX paper sometime Wednesday or Thursday morning.
EFPs act as protection from having to take delivery of physical foreign barrels, allowing the EFP buyer or seller to exchange a futures position for a physical position.
